From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Aligning MAP with procurement windows (Greenlane pilot)

Aisha / team —

Quick legal read on sequencing. High level notes (estimates assume typical counterparty speed):

- SOC2/security packet: we’ll upload our SOC2 + architecture notes today to the shared Drive. That enables procurement to complete their vendor checklist quickly (1–2 business days if they have a checklist in place).
- DPA review: often runs concurrent with MSA, but some customers prefer redlining DPA after MSA has settled. Expect 3–7 business days for standard DPA redline (depends on privacy team availability).
- MSA redline window: 7–12 business days if there are multiple commercial changes; shorter if we can limit to schedule/term edits.
- Order Form: simple execution once MSA is agreed — e-sign typically same-day when signatures are routed, but finance approvals can add 2–3 business days.

Risk items to call out:
- Data residency / audit log retention clauses in the DPA — if Greenlane requires custom retention periods, that can add a round.
- Procurement wanting proof of deletion / data export assurances for pilot (we can provide standard language).

Proposed compressed sequencing for Oct 20 sign target (rough):
- 9/22: provide SOC2 + security packet (Aisha)
- 9/22–9/24: procurement vendor review (Greenlane)
- 9/24: Redwood sends initial clean MSA + DPA (we have a standard DPA that covers EU/US; if Greenlane has bespoke needs, that diverges)
- 9/24–10/05: legal redlines loop (aim to finish by 10/05)
- 10/06–10/12: final sign-off and e-sign routing

If procurement insists on Oct 1 legal handoff, we should confirm whether Oct 20 is a hard signature date or a softer target. If hard, we can request expedited legal review from Greenlane counsel (copy Paul Norton?) to compress rounds.

I attached a short doc with redline window assumptions (MSA_redline_window.docx).

Karthik
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
